supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Shipping traffic through Strait of Hormuz rises slightly
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports Kpler tracked 10 commodity-vessel transits Wednesday, up from eight Tuesday, still below the roughly 15-vessel 10-day average.

supportingEvidence.title: Oman: temporary maritime corridor coordinated with IMO
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Omani material confirms a real navigation-restoration mechanism exists and emphasizes freedom of navigation without transit fees.

supportingEvidence.title: IMO: confirmed Middle East maritime incidents
supportingEvidence.note: IMO continues to list recent vessel damage in and near Hormuz, showing physical-security risk has not disappeared merely because traffic is rising.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters/Kpler: traffic remains below recent average and AIS coverage is incomplete
contradictingEvidence.note: The same report says traffic remains below the recent moving average and acknowledges that transponder-off vessels can be missed.

contradictingEvidence.title: IMO: recent confirmed vessel damage remains part of the operating environment
contradictingEvidence.note: Recent confirmed maritime incidents mean a higher vessel count is not equivalent to restored physical security.

falsifier: Upgrade toward NORMALIZING only if several consecutive days of independent vessel and oil-flow data move materially toward pre-war baselines while maritime incidents, tanker freight and war-risk insurance also normalize. Downgrade the recovery-momentum thesis if traffic falls back toward crisis lows or renewed attacks reverse the increase.
title: Hormuz traffic shows recovery momentum but remains below recent norms
summary: Kpler-tracked commodity-vessel traffic through Hormuz rose to 10 transits Wednesday from eight Tuesday, but remains below the roughly 15-vessel recent moving average. The data justify a momentum upgrade, not a normalization call, because AIS coverage is incomplete and physical-security risk remains present.
delta: Supersede the static severe-impairment interpretation with a two-speed state: short-term traffic momentum is improving, while absolute normalization remains unproven. Keep the pre-war physical baseline as the main normalization yardstick and the recent moving average as a momentum indicator only.
firstOrderImpacts: incrementally higher probability of near-term shipping recovery
continued downward pressure on geopolitical crude risk premium if traffic keeps improving
continued caution for tanker operators and insurers while security risk remains unresolved
secondOrderImpacts: oil prices may normalize faster than freight, insurance and refined-product logistics
short-term momentum and absolute normalization should remain separate Orbital Insight variables
alternative-data value depends on whether vessel/security telemetry improves recovery classification beyond diplomatic headlines and oil prices

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Combining pre-war absolute-flow baselines with daily vessel momentum and maritime-security telemetry will classify Hormuz recovery earlier and more accurately than diplomacy headlines or Brent/WTI alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: diplomatic reopening headlines and crude-price reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: daily Kpler/IMO/PortWatch-compatible vessel activity, absolute oil-flow estimates, maritime incidents, tanker freight, war-risk insurance and refined-product deliveries
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: 3-7 day classification accuracy for SEVERE_IMPAIRMENT / CONTESTED_REOPENING / NORMALIZING and lead time versus the public-headline baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the added telemetry layer if it does not improve held-out recovery classification or arrives too late to change a decision.
